findings.summary: The shared OCR URL helper is not the only OCR asset path builder in current source.
findings.consequence: Client-side OCR fetches and server-side OCR fetches can drift if work ID encoding, page-index formatting, or allowed-path identity changes, leaving one path requesting or allowlisting a different asset for the same Reader page.
findings.evidence: The owned helper constructs `/txt/${encodeRfc3986Segment(workId)}/ocr_${String(pageIndex).padStart(5, "0")}.html` at line 48 and is used by `app/lib/reader-facsimile-page.ts`. `server/utils/reader-ocr.ts` still constructs `/txt/${encodeURIComponent(workId)}/ocr_${filename}.html` locally before fetching and allowlisting the asset path.
findings.recommendation: Import and use `facsimileOcrUrl(workId, pageIndex)` from `server/utils/reader-ocr.ts` as the single OCR request-builder before prefixing with the content base, so SSR and client OCR fetches share validation, padding, and segment encoding.
